Subject: MedixCorp - AWS Marketplace private offer: term structuring & buyer approval windows

Hi Markus,

Following up on our conversation at the conference — MedixCorp is evaluating a Marketplace private offer for a cross-division deployment. A few specific items procurement needs clarity on before we can route internally: 

- Can Redwood support a 36-month term (three-year) private offer with a stepped discount at year 2/3? We need an example price curve (list price -> year1/year2/year3) for a multi-account deployment.
- We have five AWS payer accounts across subsidiaries. What does the buyer approval flow look like for a multi-account private offer? Does each subsidiary need to sign/approve, or can procurement sign centrally if we provide a PO referencing all account IDs?
- What evidence does Redwood require to activate an MPO (PO, signed SOW, AWS account IDs, executive approval)? Any sample checklist would help speed our procurement cycle.

I've attached our RFP matrix (Medix_RFP_Q2.xlsx) — procurement column highlights the sections relevant to terms and approval windows. Can we get a short written response + a 30-minute sync next week?

Thanks,
Jane Doe

procurement@medixcorp.com

Subject: Re: MedixCorp - AWS Marketplace private offer: term structuring & buyer approval windows

Hi Jane — thanks for the RFP and the clear list. We're well set up to support multi-account MPOs and flexible term structures. Quick summary and proposed next steps: 

1) Term/pricing options (examples):
   - Option A — 12-month committed: standard list price with volume tiers and an early-commit rebate at 12 months. Good when customers want annual budget cycles.
   - Option B — 36-month committed: 10% off list in year 1, 12% in year 2, 15% in year 3 (example curve). Can include a minimum annual commit and automatic volume true-up.

2) Multi-account approvals:
   - We typically accept a centrally issued PO that references all AWS account IDs and the payer account, provided an authorized signatory from procurement signs and confirms authority to bind all subsidiaries. In some enterprises each subsidiary requires a separate approver — we can reflect that in the MPO metadata (multiple approver emails) if needed.

3) Evidence checklist (what we need to activate):
   - Signed PO referencing Redwood MPO terms and all AWS account IDs
   - Signed Marketplace Terms (we can provide a short signature stub or DocuSign)
   - AWS payer account ID(s) and billing owner contact
   - Optional: SOW for professional services (if included)

I attached a short checklist that we use internally (Redwood_MPO_Checklist.pdf). Can we do a 30-minute sync Monday 5/21 at 10am PT? If that works we'll draft a sample MPO term sheet and a pre-filled DocuSign for you to review.

Best,
Markus Klein
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0128

Karthik, Irene — forwarding the Medix RFP note from Jane (procurement). Highlights and asks: 

- Customer explicitly wants a 36-month structure with stepped discounts and needs clarity on multi-account approvals.
- Finance will want to know if we can protect against churn (minimum annual commitment / true-ups) and what concession authority you have for multi-year deals.
- Irene, can you confirm co-sell entitlements for a 3-year MPO (marketplace listing + co-sell benefits)? Any additional AWS PR requirements?

I think we can propose Option B as the primary path but leave an annual true-up clause. Can you both weigh in before I send the sample term sheet to Jane?

Thanks — Markus
